Write a connectivity report's source, so you can render it yourself

Source: R/generate-report.R
write_connectivity_report.Rd

Writes the report as a Quarto document you own a copy of, next to the data it draws. Open it, change it, render it. render_connectivity_report() renders it the way the package does, and generate_connectivity_report() does both steps at once when the source isn't wanted.

Usage

write_connectivity_report(x, path = NULL)

Arguments

x

A connectivity_report_data object from connectivity_report_data().

path

File to write, ending in .qmd. Defaults to the species and today's date, in the working directory. The directory must already exist.

Value

The absolute path of the .qmd, invisibly.

Details

Two files are written: path, and the analysis beside it as <name>-data.rds. The document reads that file by name, so the two travel together. Moving one without the other breaks the render.

See also

render_connectivity_report() to render it, generate_connectivity_report() to do both.

Examples

# \donttest{
report_data <- connectivity_report_data(
  habitat = example_habitat(),
  barrier = example_barrier(),
  species = "Blue Tongue Lizard",
  interpatch_distance = 20,
  verbose = FALSE
)

qmd <- write_connectivity_report(
  report_data,
  file.path(tempdir(), "lizard-report.qmd")
)

readLines(qmd, n = 5)
#> [1] "---"                                   
#> [2] "title: \"Habitat connectivity report\""
#> [3] "date: today"                           
#> [4] "params:"                               
#> [5] "  report_data: null"                   
# }
